title: Hosted API demo - chat/text generation basics (streaming, params, retries)

Agreed next steps include sharing pricing, security docs, trial API key, and a short benchmark run with sample prompts.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-22
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Aisha Patel (Rose Retail PM), Tom Nguyen (Rose Lead Eng), Liam O'Connor (Rose CTO)

Auto-generated Summary: (may be imperfect)
Redwood hosted API demo focusing on chat/text basics including streaming, parameters and retry logic. Customer asked about latency and cost and compliance questions. Next steps: pricing + trial + benchmark.

00:00 - Maya: okay hi everyone, thanks for taking the time today, uh this is Maya from Redwood Inference, I'm joined by Diego on the engineering side. How's everyone doing?
00:07 - Aisha: good thanks Maya, excited to see this, thanks for fitting us in.
00:10 - Diego: hey all, quick agenda - we'll run through hosted API for chat and text generation, show streaming, key params, and how to handle retries safely. then we can take questions and cover security briefly.
00:22 - Tom: great, we're primarily interested in a chat assistant for product search and personalized recommendations, and we care a lot about tail latency.
00:30 - Liam: and from infra side we need to understand data retention and SOC2 stuff, plus whether we need dedicated or hosted.
00:36 - Maya: perfect, that's exactly what we'll touch on. quick quals - what's your current stack for inference? are you calling OpenAI already or self-hosting?
00:44 - Aisha: right now we have a small experiment hitting OpenAI for search summarization and some prompts, but costs are creeping up; also want better control over latency and routing to region.
00:55 - Diego: understood. okay jumping in - here's a simple curl example to call Redwood hosted chat endpoint. (screen share)
01:05 - Diego: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"model":"rw-medium-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"find me shoes under 100 dollars in size 9"}],"stream":true}'
01:26 - Aisha: oh you support streaming? that's good for our UI to render tokens as they arrive.
01:29 - Diego: yes, we do streaming over chunked transfer, you get event-stream style chunks. we also support a websocket option if you need bi-directional. small caveat - streaming does slightly change how you think about retries because partial responses might have been sent.
01:45 - Tom: can you elaborate on retries - we worry about duplicate actions if an API call times out and we retry.
01:50 - Diego: yeah, great question. we recommend idempotency keys for create-like calls; for pure generation we suggest client-side dedupe logic plus server-side request ids. our SDKs set a request id header automatically, and for higher-level flows we advise an at-most-once pattern with a short timeout and exponential backoff.
02:12 - Diego: also, for streaming specifically, clients often set a short initial timeout and then let the stream continue; if you reconnect you can request from a token offset using the kv-cache/continuation token feature, although note the auto transcript sometimes writes 'K V cache' in docs.
02:30 - Liam: kv-cache continuation token - is that available on hosted? any privacy implications?
02:34 - Diego: yes hosted supports prefix caching and session keys but we don't persist customer prompts to serve other customers. you can enable or disable cache per-tenant; for regulated workloads Redwood Private or Dedicated gives additional isolation.
02:45 - Maya: to event - cost/latency tradeoff question, what do you typically recommend?
02:49 - Diego: generally you pick a model and quantization profile for inference - lower-cost quantized variants are great for high qps. for low-latency SLOs we suggest smaller sequence lengths, prefix caching to avoid re-tokenizing history, and streaming to start showing tokens earlier. batching helps throughput but increases latency, so we tune per-route. Redwood Optimize also has recommendations to pick batch sizes and quantization per workload. (note: sometimes our docs say Red Wood Optimize)
03:18 - Aisha: how about generation parameters - we want consistent helpful results. what's best practice for temperature, top_p and max_tokens?
03:24 - Diego: for deterministic answers lower temperature (0-0.2) and maybe top_p 0.8-1.0 for more conservative sampling. max_tokens you set based on expected length; we also support stop sequences. for chat, we recommend role-based system prompts and a short user history in the request to bound compute.
03:45 - Tom: do you have SDKs we can drop into our node backend?
03:48 - Maya: yes, we have official SDKs for Python, Node, and Go. Diego will show a quick node example.
03:54 - Diego: here's node: const client = new Redwood({apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY}); const res = await client.chat.generate({model:'rw-medium-1', messages:[{role:'user',content:'...'}], stream:true}); res.on('data', chunk => { /* append token */ });
04:12 - Aisha: nice. and retries in the SDK?
04:15 - Diego: SDK implements automatic retries with exponential backoff for 5xx and connection errors, but not for 4xxs. you can override strategy or add idempotency keys. for streaming endpoints the SDK will try a resumable approach for transient disconnects.
04:28 - Liam: do you expose metrics for token usage and latencies? we need to map costs to product teams.
04:33 - Maya: yes Console gives per-route token and latency breakdowns, plus trace hooks. you can export to prometheus or our logs.
04:42 - Tom: what's the rate limit shape - per-key, per-account?
04:45 - Diego: hosted has per-key rate limits and account-level quotas; we can adjust for trials. for sustained enterprise throughput we recommend Redwood Dedicated.
04:55 - Aisha: pricing - can you send a sheet? we currently care about per-1k token charges and embedding vs generation costs.
05:00 - Maya: absolutely, I'll send the hosted pricing sheet and an estimate for your expected volume.
05:05 - Diego: quick demo of streaming in the UI - (share) live chat where responses stream token by token into a message box. you can configure stop tokens and finalization callbacks.
05:20 - Diego: show param slider for temperature and top_p in Console - changes reflected in API payload.
05:30 - Aisha: nice, helps product iterate.
05:33 - Tom: security compliance - SOC2, SSO, KMS. can you point us at docs?
05:38 - Maya: yes we have SOC2 Type II report, SSO via SAML/Okta and KMS integrations. I'll share the security pack. for dedicated or private deployments we also offer customer-managed keys and audit log export.
05:55 - Liam: good. what about data residency - do you support region pinning?
05:59 - Diego: hosted has region endpoints in us-east, us-west, and eu-west. Dedicated and Private let you control region fully.
06:08 - Aisha: back to the retry topic - can you show an example of idempotency header?
06:12 - Diego: sure - we recommend X-Idempotency-Key: uuid and the SDK sets it automatically for non-streaming calls. For streaming, you often use session ids and continuation tokens.
06:25 - Tom: how does billing count partial streams? e.g., if we time out and reconnect do we get billed twice?
06:31 - Maya: billing is per-token consumed server-side. if a retry causes repeated generation you'll be billed for the tokens generated. that's why we advise careful retry/backoff and idempotency when doing expensive generations.
06:43 - Aisha: can we set hard token limits to avoid runaway bills?
06:46 - Diego: yes you can set per-route max_tokens and account quotas. Console also supports alerts when spend exceeds thresholds.
06:55 - Maya: ok i'm going to demo a short sample prompt and show streaming then show turning off streaming for full response.
07:00 - Diego: request with stream:true - tokens begin flowing after about 120ms on rw-medium-1 for short prompts; for larger models or long contexts latency will increase. (note: numbers are approximate)
07:18 - Aisha: 120ms sounds great - that's in p50 or p95?
07:21 - Diego: that's p50 for simple prompts; p95 depends on workload and region, and we can run a benchmark for your prompts to get accurate numbers.
07:30 - Tom: benchmark - we'd like a short run with our 10 prompts and measure p50/p95 and cost.
07:34 - Maya: agreed - that's in next steps.
07:38 - Diego: showing code: python example to set temperature and stop sequences, and how to parse streamed SSE events. (shows code)
07:50 - Aisha: any gotchas about tokenization differences? we have some pre-tokenized inputs in product search.
07:55 - Diego: yes tokenization can vary across models; we expose token counting in SDKs so you can measure before sending. also prefix caching reduces repeated tokenization cost.
08:08 - Liam: curious about throughput - if we have bursts during peak sale days, can hosted handle spikes?
08:14 - Maya: hosted autoscaling handles spikes but if you need guaranteed throughput we recommend Dedicated reservations or a hybrid model. reserved capacity gives predictable latency and cost.
08:24 - Tom: and what about end-to-end encryption for transit and at-rest?
08:27 - Diego: TLS in transit, at-rest encryption via customer-managed KMS is available on Private and Dedicated; hosted supports platform-managed keys by default and can integrate with your KMS for enterprise plans.
08:40 - Aisha: what about retention of prompts for safety/debugging?
08:44 - Maya: by default we retain logs for 30 days for troubleshooting; you can opt out and enable no-retention mode for sensitive workloads. we'll include retention settings in the security doc.
08:55 - Liam: any references for SLA and uptime?
08:58 - Maya: hosted has a 99.9% uptime SLA on enterprise plans; Dedicated has higher SLAs depending on contract. I'll attach SLA docs.
09:08 - Diego: quick note on model catalog - we publish verified performance profiles for each model (latency/cost) in Console so you can pick the right one.
09:16 - Aisha: let's talk about integration timeline - we'd like to pilot in 2 weeks and decide in 6 weeks.
09:21 - Maya: sounds reasonable. I'll follow up with a trial key and timeline suggestions.
09:26 - Tom: anything else on retry semantics? what about circuit breakers?
09:29 - Diego: we recommend client defensive measures - per-route circuit breakers, short timeouts, exponential backoff, and server-side rate limiting to protect throughput. our SDKs provide pluggable hooks for that.
09:40 - Aisha: do you support function calling or structured outputs? we need product JSON responses for downstream systems.
09:45 - Diego: yes we support function/tool calling patterns and structured output schema enforcement so the model returns JSON. Works well with chat flows.
09:53 - Maya: ok let's recap action items and next steps.
09:56 - Maya: action items - I'll send pricing and security pack; Diego will attach quickstart and scripts; Tom to share prompts; Liam to give security contact. We'll run a benchmark and reconvene.
10:08 - Liam: thanks all, this was helpful.
10:10 - Aisha: thanks Maya and Diego. we'll look out for the trial key.
10:13 - Maya: great, I'll send notes and next steps in the CRM.
